items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: I saw one of my neighbors, Jack Brown.

ctx.x: So I stood there and stood there, waving and waving, and I'm getting wet and the rain is getting harder, so I finally decided that I better do something -- so I took my bass drum, put it under my arm, and I took my tom toms and put that over my arm and with the drum case, and I picked it all up -- I don't know where I got the strength from -- but I picked all of this stuff up and walked from 40th Street to 46th Street, near Broadway to Capital Studio -- soaking wet.

I'm cursing, I'm mad; you could fry an egg on my head I was so mad, and I'm cursing the cab drivers and everything else, and I said, 'I'm gonna buy me a car.' So the next morning, the next day I didn't have a recording session until that night, so I came downstairs and I saw one of my neighbors, Jack Brown. And I said to Jack, I said, 'Hey, Jack, do you know anything about cars?' He said, 'A little bit', and I said, 'Well, look, I want to buy a car, and I just looked in the paper here and I see they got a 1953…
it's all right?" So he says, "Yeah, I'll go with you; I got nothing to do -- I'm off today."
